name: Omega-3 fish oil capsule
identity: Soft gelatine capsule of about 1 g concentrated sea fish or salmon oil with 300 to 500 mg omega-3 fatty acids, as dm, Rossmann and pharmacies sell it; the dose is one capsule.
rule: Per 100 g of the product, each value is the median of the labels below that declare it, and a value enters only when at least three declare it. A fish oil capsule's label states its content as oil (1,000 or 1,400 mg sea fish oil per capsule, or the oil's share of the capsule), and by that it declares the oil's nutrients: the oil mass is the fat, its energy is 9 kcal per gram, and the oil carries 0 g carbohydrate and 0 g protein; the gelatine shell is left unstated. The two labels with a full table per 100 g, Mivolis and altapharma, are the check on that understatement: they put the shell at 18 to 21 g protein and 4.5 to 7 g carbohydrate per 100 g, a quarter of a gram of protein per capsule, so the capsule's energy, the point of logging it, is within a few percent either way. EPA, DHA and vitamin E are not tracked and stay out. The capsule weight is the pack's net content divided by its count. Labels read on 2026-10-30 from dm.de, rossmann.de and shop-apotheke.com product pages; nothing a label leaves out becomes zero.
